newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia hikes import tariffs to plug fiscal hole.
newsitem.headline: Colombia hikes import tariffs to plug fiscal hole.

text.p: The Colombian government said it was temporarily raising its import tariffs in a bid to raise sorely needed revenues to plug a gaping fiscal deficit running at about 4 percent of gross domestic product.
The increase was announced by outgoing Foreign Trade Minister Morris Harf who said it could bring in about 265 billion pesos if it remained in effect over a 12-month period.
The move was triggered by a Constitutional Court ruling Wednesday night overturning the government's three-month-old economic emergency plan, Harf told a news conference.
The court ruling could prevent the government from collecting about 600 billion pesos in new tax revenues this year.
Harf said the tariff increase would remain in effect for at least 90 days, after which it would be subject to renewal by the government's High Council on Foreign Trade.
Import tariffs vary widely in Colombia, but Harf said Thursday's measure would raise the lowest from 5 percent to 7 percent and the highest, on vehicle imports, from 35 to 40 percent.
